title: GPU_ORDER's "cheapest-first" comment is stale - our own RAM floor excludes the two cheap cards
description:
UMBRELLA: MPI-558 - The smoke-gate runner: a Pod-side twin and a stale GPU order (consolidation sweep 2026-08-14). Members and phase order: tasks/MPI-558/plan.md.

SIBLING: MPI-502 - same file (scripts/smoke-workflows.mjs), same smoke-gate track. Do both in one pass rather than touching the runner twice.

scripts/smoke-workflows.mjs GPU_ORDER is commented 'cheapest-first by measured availability', but across THREE consecutive runs on 2026-08-10 the L4 refused, the RTX 3090 refused, and only the 4090 took it - every time. That is not availability noise, it is our own MIN_RAM_GB = 48 excluding those host classes in EU-RO-1 (the volume pins the datacenter). Every run pays two pointless refusal round-trips to rediscover it. Cheap (a refusal rents nothing, and the MPI-450 fallback fix means it no longer kills the run) but the comment now misleads whoever reads it next. DO NOT 'fix' this by lowering the floor blind - 48GB exists because weights spill to system RAM on a 24GB card. Either re-measure the order under the real floor, or drop the floor only if footprint.js no longer needs it. Also worth knowing: `ramFloorMissed: true` is NOT evidence the floor caused a refusal - remotePodLifecycle.js:859 sets that flag on ANY failure of the RAM-floor GraphQL create path. RunPod's own message is the signal.
